reason: This passage (Exodus 3) frames the Hebrew liberation from Egypt primarily through religious and cosmic dimensions rather than political struggle. The entire narrative is structured as a theophany—God directly revealing Himself to Moses at the burning bush, establishing His identity as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and issuing a divine command. While oppression (לַחַץ) and the cry (צַעֲקַת) of the Israelites are mentioned as motivations, they are presented as phenomena observed by God, not as a political movement. Critically, the purpose of liberation is explicitly stated in religious terms: 'you shall serve God on this mountain' (תַּעַבְדוּן אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִים עַל הָהָר הַזֶּה). The narrative emphasizes divine agency, God's will, and religious covenant rather than human political struggle or military action. The Hebrews are passive recipients of God's liberation, not active participants in a political fight.
